subject.title: Context pruning mode 'off' not preventing compactions (Anthropic API key, cache-ttl smart defaults)

question: Should OpenClaw add a supported hard-limit-only or fully-off automatic compaction mode, and should compaction entries persist a closed trigger reason?
rationale: Current main already honors pruning off, but the remaining request changes compaction safety semantics, user-visible config, and persisted transcript metadata.

options.title: Define hard-limit semantics
options.body: Add an approved config contract that preserves overflow recovery while disabling threshold/safeguard compaction, with docs, tests, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep current compaction policy
options.body: Treat fully-off automatic compaction as unsupported and limit follow-up work to verified false low-context triggers plus clearer diagnostics.

options.title: Wait for current Anthropic proof
options.body: Require live current-main Anthropic evidence before accepting a new compaction contract beyond the related subagent-wake report.

recommendation.title: Define hard-limit semantics
recommendation.body: Add an approved config contract that preserves overflow recovery while disabling threshold/safeguard compaction, with docs, tests, and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and adjacent compaction/runtime history put this owner closest to the config and compaction safety boundary.
